target_customer: Online shoppers for electronics and appliances, with authorized retailers as the paying side
problem: Shoppers spend time hunting for deals and cannot easily get retailers to compete on price for a specific product.
business_model: Marketplace where shoppers name a price and retailers accept; take from retailer sales (rate not stated)

founders.name: Andrew Kurland
founders.role: Co-founder, CEO (listed as CTO on YC page)
founders.background_notes: No background found in opened sources.

founders.name: Joe Marrapodi
prior_employers: Talent negotiation work with celebrities, employer not named
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch July 2014; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Amazon
competitors.what: General online retail price benchmark Greentoe aimed to beat

competitors.name: eBay
competitors.what: Marketplace price benchmark named alongside Amazon

technical_complexity.rationale: Offer routing to retailers and payment commitment; standard marketplace engineering plus retailer integrations, with an iOS app added in October 2014.

defensibility.rationale: Value depends on retailer relationships with authorized sellers; the model was copyable and no network effect is sourced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying the model; the company continues to operate and bought Discount Bandit in 2023.

market_need_then: Founders said they started it after spending too much time hunting for online deals; the Priceline model was cited as proof of name-your-price demand in travel. No demand figures found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Consumer empowerment: shoppers set the price

branding.community_and_virality: Local TV and blog coverage in 2013 and 2014 (ABC stations, Techlicious) described the concept; no evidence of fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Unusual name with no sourced origin, modest press on the concept rather than the brand.

outcome_analysis: Greentoe is still operating a name-your-price marketplace for electronics a decade after YC, with a 2023 acquisition of Discount Bandit and a claimed half billion dollars in e-commerce volume by its own account. Funding found was small (about 1.5 million dollars across two seeds), so it appears to have grown without large venture rounds, though it did not become a venture-scale outlier.
notes: Seed amounts conflict by source: 500K (SoCalTech Nov 2013), 1M (TechCrunch Oct 2014), Wellfound 1.8M and CB Insights 520K total are unverified aggregators. The 1M round investor list from StartupIntros (Dave McClure, Richard Chen, Eric Witte) is a single aggregator, not recorded. PriceWaiter was named in a 2014 article seen only as a search snippet, not opened, so it is not listed. Priceline is the model analog, not recorded as a competitor. Greentoe founded 2012 per YC page; the 2013 round predates the S14 batch.
